title: Lumenary Materials
subtitle: Materials science from atoms and crystals to the semiconductors, batteries and AI-discovered materials of 2026: structure, processing, mechanical behaviour, the families of materials, functional materials, characterisation and computation.
description: Lumenary Materials is the materials-science subject of Lumenary Scientia, free and open source like the others. It starts with no experience at all — why steel bends and glass shatters — and climbs through bonding and crystal structure, diffraction and defects, diffusion, phase diagrams and processing, mechanical behaviour and failure, metals, ceramics, polymers, composites and biomaterials, electronic, optical and magnetic materials, and the microscopes and simulations materials scientists use, to the battery, quantum and sustainable materials and the AI-assisted discovery of 2026.

Every lesson teaches with ideas first and calculation second. Calculations and simulations — packing fractions, diffraction patterns, diffusion profiles, phase fractions, band structures, a small molecular dynamics run — are in Python with NumPy, and every block with a **Run in browser** button runs there, with nothing to install. A lesson says *Code tested* only when all of its code passed. Lumenary Materials shares ground with [Lumenary Chemistry](/en/chemistry/), [Lumenary ME](/en/me/) and [Lumenary EE](/en/ee/), and links to them where they meet.

Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human materials scientist. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Where a laboratory, database or society has published the primary source — a paper, a phase diagram, a materials database — the lesson links to it rather than retelling it.

levels.title: What things are made of
levels.summary: No experience needed, from about age 11. The materials around us, how atoms and bonds give materials their properties, materials through human history, and choosing and reusing materials well.

levels.title: Atoms, bonds and crystals
levels.summary: The structure underneath every property: bonding in solids, crystal structures, X-ray diffraction, defects and dislocations, and glasses and nanomaterials.

levels.title: How materials form and change
levels.summary: Atoms on the move: diffusion, phase diagrams, phase transformations, and how processing and heat treatment set a material's structure.

levels.title: Mechanical behaviour
levels.summary: How materials deform and fail: elasticity, plasticity and strengthening, fracture and toughness, and fatigue, creep and corrosion.

levels.title: Families of materials
levels.summary: The great classes of engineering materials and what each is good for: metals and alloys, ceramics and glasses, polymers, composites, and biomaterials.

levels.title: Electronic, optical and magnetic materials
levels.summary: Materials chosen for what they do rather than what they bear: electronic structure and bands, semiconductors, dielectrics and ferroelectrics, magnetic materials, optical materials, and superconductors.

levels.title: Characterisation and computation
levels.summary: How materials scientists see and predict: microscopy, spectroscopy and thermal analysis, atomistic simulation, density functional theory, and multiscale modelling.

levels.title: The frontier of materials science
levels.summary: Where the field is moving in 2026, with links to the primary sources: AI-assisted materials discovery, battery materials, two-dimensional and quantum materials, sustainable materials, and metamaterials.
